sources.title: AFI Catalog: The Untouchables (1987)
supports: Kevin Costner is credited as Eliot Ness; Brian De Palma directed and David Mamet wrote.
The feature was suggested by the 1959–63 television series and books connected to Ness.
The screenplay presents Ness differently from the television portrayal, and the screen Catherine Ness and daughter were fictionalized.
sources.limits: AFI supports role credits and production history, but the film is a dramatization of a real person. The AFI page contains an erroneous De Palma/De Niro Mean Streets collaboration claim, which this report does not use.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 60th Academy Awards (1988)
supports: The Untouchables received four nominations and one win.
Sean Connery won Actor in a Supporting Role.
Art Direction, Costume Design, and Ennio Morricone’s Original Score were the other nominations.
sources.limits: The awards ledger supports outcomes and categories, not historical accuracy or plot. Connery’s win is for Jim Malone, not an award for Costner’s Eliot Ness.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: The Princess Bride (1987)
supports: Cary Elwes is credited as Westley; Rob Reiner directed and William Goldman wrote.
Goldman wrote both the 1973 novel and the screenplay.
The adaptation closely follows the novel with selected changes, including the Pit of Despair in place of the novel’s Zoo of Death.
sources.limits: This record supports credits and adaptation history; Westley and the story world are fictional, so its synopsis is not historical evidence.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 60th Academy Awards (1988)
supports: The Princess Bride received one Academy Award nomination.
The nomination was for Original Song: ‘Storybook Love,’ with music and lyrics by Willy DeVille.
sources.limits: This ledger supports a song nomination only; it is not an acting award for Cary Elwes and does not establish plot or adaptation details.
